args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions following the deploy of v2.3.1 (error rate ~18%, healthy=false in us-east, us-west, eu-west).

Action taken: rolled production back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production (v2.2.9 also healthy; v2.3.1-rc was unhealthy in staging and never released to production).

Note: the first rollback attempt partially failed — the rollout halted after us-east due to an orchestrator error, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollback to v2.3.0 across all three regions.

Current state: all regions at v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate ~0.2%.

Follow-up: investigate why v2.3.1 failed health checks before any redeploy attempt. Redeploying a version that has never been healthy in production would require change-manager approval.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
Done. The incident did get created (INC-0001) despite the timeout, so no retry was needed.

## Summary

**Situation:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 with `healthy: false` and an 18% error rate across us-east, us-west, and eu-west.

**Target selection:** Release history showed two healthy production releases (v2.2.9 and v2.3.0). I chose **v2.3.0** as the most recent release healthy in production. I excluded v2.3.1-rc — it was unhealthy *and* only ever deployed to staging, so it was never a valid production rollback target.

**Rollback:**
- First attempt returned `partial_failure`: the rollout halted after us-east on an orchestrator error, leaving the service in a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1).
- Retried, which completed the rollout to v2.3.0 in all three regions.

**Verification:** `version: v2.3.0` in all regions, `healthy: true`, error rate down from 18% → 0.2%.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2 on checkout-api, documenting the v2.3.1 failure, the rollback target choice, the partial-failure/retry, and the post-rollback state.

**Two things worth flagging:**
1. v2.3.1 remains an unresolved bad artifact — it should be investigated before anyone redeploys it. Per policy, deploying a version that has never been healthy in production requires change-manager approval, so a redeploy attempt cannot proceed without that sign-off.
2. The orchestrator error that caused the partial rollout halt is itself a reliability concern; it's noted in the incident, but you may want a separate follow-up with the platform team since a failed rollback mid-incident leaves production in a mixed-version state.
